messages:
helen: Follow-up from postmortem INC-9404 — most pages came in during late-night deploy window. We need a safe after-hours suppression policy that preserves ownership and doesn't hide real outages.
omar: Noted. Two quick goals: reduce wakeups by >50% during quiet hours, and ensure at least one oncall pager per owning team when their resources are involved.
vince: Suggestion: timebox suppression (quiet-hours 22:00-07:00 local) + owner-affinity keys so each team still gets a single page. Also add an absolute-bypass for high severity (errors/min > 1500 or distinct_hosts > 8).
jess: I like timebox + owner-affinity. We also need a clear timeline and metrics to validate. Propose metric exports: alerts.suppressed.count, alerts.paged.count, alerts.repaged_after_suppression.count, and alerts.suppression.window_seconds.
helen: Draft rule behaviour: 1) If within quiet-hours AND event classified as "noise" by pattern (deploy_tag=true OR transient_socket) -> route to Slack for 10m 2) If same fingerprint + owner appears again within 10m -> deliver 1 pager to owner then suppress further for 30m 3) If absolute_bypass triggers, bypass suppression immediately.
omar: How do we classify "noise" reliably? We should use deploy_tag + recent deploys list + known transient error signatures. Maybe a small ML classifier later, but start with heuristics.
vince: Implementation sketch for alertproxy middleware:
```
if in_quiet_hours(service.region):
  if is_deploy_noise(event) or is_transient_sig(event):
    deliver = slack
    set_suppression(fingerprint+owner, ttl=30m, note="quiet-hour-deploy")
  else:
    evaluate_normal_paging()
else:
  evaluate_normal_paging()
# absolute bypass
if rate > 1500 or distinct_hosts > 8:
  deliver = pager
```
jess: Rollout plan: (A) push middleware to staging, (B) run synthetic bursts during off-hours in staging for 48h, (C) canary to one region overnight for 72h, (D) global. Revert if repaged_after_suppression > 0.5% during canary or missed critical alerts.
helen: Owners & ETAs: omar (middleware + heuristics + metrics) ETA Thu EOD; vince (synthetic bursts + dashboards) ETA Mon; jess (runbook + deploy-tag coordination with deploy team) ETA Tue next week.
omar: I'll add a small log-sampling stream of suppressed events (1%) to a retention bucket so we can audit missed signals. Also will tag suppressed events with pm_ticket=PM-6130 and suppression_reason.
vince: For measurement, we should compute pages_per_hour_before/after and suppressed_ratio_by_owner. I'll add Grafana dashboards and a short alert if suppressed_ratio_by_owner > 0.7 (means we're suppressing too much for a team).
jess: We also need an explicit manual override in the oncall console to disable quiet-hours suppression per-service for emergencies. I'll add the toggle and a short process doc.
incident-bot: Note: Created follow-up task ACT-9404-QH and assigned to omar, vince, jess.
helen: Action items recap:
- omar: implement quiet-hours detection + suppression middleware, export metrics and sample logs (due Thu EOD)
- vince: synthetic traffic harness + dashboards + canary automation (due Mon)
- jess: update runbooks, add override toggle, coordinate with deploy team for deploy tags (due Tue)
We'll meet Fri 09:00 PT to review staging metrics and decide canary timing. Any objections?
omar: No objections, starting the PR today.
vince: I'll schedule synthetic runs for Thu night in staging and post logs here.
jess: I'll draft the runbook changes and share a short checklist for the oncall team. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall this week helen -> primary, omar -> secondary. Use /incident link INC-9404 when testing.
